# How many skeins of yarn for a blanket?

> Scale total yarn yardage and whole skeins directly from a washed swatch in your actual stitch, then sanity-check against standard blanket sizes and yarn weights.

## Calculator
- [Open the calculator](https://tallysprig.com/): US throw: a 50 × 60 in blanket scaled from a 4 × 4 in swatch using 12 yd needs 2,475 yd with 10% extra (13 skeins of 200 yd). Metric: a 120 × 160 cm blanket scaled from a 10 × 10 cm swatch using 10 m needs 2,112 m with 10% extra (11 skeins of 200 m).

## Guide
- [How to work out how many skeins of yarn a blanket needs](https://tallysprig.com/guide/): step-by-step measuring, common mistakes, and ordering checklist.

## Formula and method
Base yarn = (blanket width × blanket length) / (swatch width × swatch height) × swatch yarn × strands; Skeins = ceiling(base yarn × (1 + extra / 100) / length per skein).

Divide finished blanket area by measured swatch area to find how many swatch units make up the blanket. Multiply by yarn consumed in one swatch and by strands held together, add your border/safety allowance, divide by single-skein length, and round up to whole skeins.

## Limits
Measure the swatch after the same washing or blocking planned for the blanket. Enter single-strand length in swatch yarn when strands > 1; if your measured swatch length already sums all strands, keep strands at 1. Wide borders, stitch changes, and tension drift alter total yardage.

## Standard blanket dimensions and typical worsted (#4) yarn estimates

Illustrative ranges for medium worsted-weight (#4) yarn. Crochet typically uses 25% to 30% more yarn than plain knitting; always verify with your own swatch.

| Blanket size | US dimensions | Metric dimensions | Approx. yardage (#4 worsted) | Approx. 200-yd skeins |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lovey / security | 12 × 12 in | 30 × 30 cm | 150–250 yd | 1–2 skeins |
| Baby / crib | 30 × 36 in | 76 × 91 cm | 800–1,100 yd | 5–6 skeins |
| Stroller / toddler | 35 × 45 in | 89 × 114 cm | 1,200–1,600 yd | 6–8 skeins |
| Throw / afghan | 50 × 60 in | 127 × 152 cm | 2,200–3,000 yd | 11–15 skeins |
| Twin bed | 66 × 90 in | 168 × 229 cm | 4,000–4,800 yd | 20–24 skeins |
| Queen bed | 90 × 90 in | 229 × 229 cm | 5,400–6,500 yd | 27–33 skeins |

## Step by step
1. Knit or crochet a swatch at least 4 × 4 in (10 × 10 cm) using the exact stitch pattern, yarn, and needle or hook size planned for the blanket.
2. Wash, dry, or block the swatch the same way you will care for the finished blanket, then measure its relaxed width and height.
3. Find how much yarn the swatch consumed by unraveling and measuring it, or by weighing the swatch on a gram scale and converting with the ball band weight-to-yardage ratio.
4. Enter your target blanket dimensions, single-skein yardage from the label, number of strands held together, and a 10% to 15% allowance for borders and joins.

## Common mistakes
- Relying solely on a generic yarn-weight chart. Crochet stitches often consume 25% to 30% more yarn than stockinette knitting of the same dimensions.
- Leaving out border edging. A multi-round crochet border on a large blanket can easily take one to two extra skeins.
- Comparing skeins instead of total yardage when substituting yarn brands. Two worsted-weight skeins can differ by more than 100 yards.
- Buying skeins from different dye lots. Even subtle shade shifts become obvious across a wide flat blanket.

## Worked examples
### Example 1
Metric: a 120 × 160 cm blanket scaled from a 10 × 10 cm swatch using 10 m needs 2,112 m with 10% extra (11 skeins of 200 m).

### Example 2
US throw: a 50 × 60 in blanket scaled from a 4 × 4 in swatch using 12 yd needs 2,475 yd with 10% extra (13 skeins of 200 yd).
